decision.rationale: All 6 candidates are direct matches for abdominal aortic aneurysm with aligned trait_reported/trait_efo and diagnosis-style phenotyping_reported. PGS000753 is preferred because it is from a disease-focused AAA genetics study (Circulation; Million Veteran Program context) and provides a PRS-comparable effect size (OR per SD 1.37, 95% CI 1.30–1.44) with basic covariates (age, sex, PCs), which is more directly informative about PRS contribution than the other candidates that mainly report full-model AUROC/C-index or partial-r. However, the overall evidence remains limited/heterogeneous: several alternatives are from framework/portability-style efforts (PGS001784, PGS002054) or report only full-model discrimination with unknown covariates (PGS003429, PGS003972), and PGS003973 reports a high C-index (0.882) but this is a full model including age/sex and is not a PGS-only metric; thus cross-model performance comparability is weak and prevents a high-confidence direct winner.

All four candidates are direct/near-direct matches for alcohol dependence via alcohol use disorder/problematic alcohol use, with endpoint fidelity supported by phenotyping_reported (DSM-5 AUD criteria count for PGS000201/PGS000202; AUD diagnosis for PGS002738/PGS002739). Among them, PGS002738 is the best-supported because it is explicitly mapped to trait_efo="alcohol dependence" and provides the strongest visible discriminative evidence (OR top 10% vs rest = 1.96 [1.54–2.51]) in a European evaluation sample (n=7,900), whereas PGS000201/PGS000202 only report small incremental ΔR² values (0.01192 and 0.00456) and PGS002739 is evaluated only in African American/Afro-Caribbean (less directly comparable without a specified deployment ancestry) with a smaller OR (1.76). The main limitation is that none of the candidates report PRS-only AUROC/R², covariates are unknown for PGS002738/PGS002739 (reducing comparability), and the remaining candidates are close enough in endpoint alignment that the choice cannot be considered high-certainty from the provided metadata alone.

All three candidates are direct matches to the target EFO (alcoholic liver cirrhosis) with broadly aligned reported traits. PGS001777 is best supported on PRS-relevant evidence because it reports a strong risk-gradient effect size (OR top 20% vs bottom 20% = 6.18, with CI) alongside an AUROC (0.671) in European validation, and it comes from a disease-focused cirrhosis prediction study. PGS000704 reports only a full-model C-index (0.711) with basic covariates and a modest per-SD HR (1.18), but lacks PRS-only metrics and appears to be from a broad biomarker genetics paper, making its discrimination less clearly attributable to the PRS. PGS004913 is disease-focused and endpoint-aligned but provides limited comparable discrimination evidence (R²=0.029; no AUROC) and has wide uncertainty on the reported OR (top vs bottom deciles). Overall confidence is limited because none of the candidates provides clear PRS-only AUROC/R² and the available metrics are not fully comparable across studies (time-to-event C-index vs case-control AUROC vs R²).

All 19 candidates are direct matches to angina pectoris (trait_efo=angina pectoris) with generally aligned phenotyping (Angina / ICD10 I20 / PheCode 411.3 / time-to-event angina). Among models with PRS-comparable metrics, the snpnet models from the pan-trait UKB framework ("across 813 traits") provide explicit PGS-only performance; PGS001261 (Angina pectoris time-to-event) has the highest reported PGS-only AUROC (0.58233) and PGS R2 (no covariates) (0.01228) among those, and its PGS-only R2 remains well below the provided heritability ceiling (h2_obs≈0.009–0.014; liability h2≈0.134), supporting metric plausibility. However, confidence is limited because these snpnet scores are explicitly from a pan-trait framework that domain guidance warns often generalizes poorly, and several newer ICD10/PheCode-aligned models (e.g., LDpred2/RFDiseasemetaPRS and MVP-based ldpred/prscs/prscsx) lack PRS-only AUC/R2 in the visible metadata, preventing a clean, high-confidence comparison; some also report only full-model C-index or OR without clear PRS-only discrimination.

All 9 candidates are direct matches to ankylosing spondylitis by trait_efo and phenotyping_reported. Among them, PGS001267 provides the clearest PRS-comparable performance evidence: it reports both PGS-only AUROC (0.7265) and PGS-only R² (0.0988), plus full-model AUROC with only basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs). Its PGS-only R² is also below the provided EUR liability-scale heritability ceiling (h2_liability=0.3993), passing the sanity-check. Competing UKB framework sibling PGS001268 has slightly higher metrics but uses a time-to-event endpoint (phenotyping_reported: TTE ankylosing spondylitis), which is a noted endpoint-fidelity warning for a generic disease target; the remaining candidates either come from portability/framework studies with only partial-correlation metrics (PGS001876/PGS002089) or report only full-model AUROC with unknown covariates in a small EAS validation (PGS003420–PGS003424), making cross-model comparability limited. Overall, a direct-match exists, but the best choice remains sub-optimal because the top candidates are framework-derived and the non-framework options lack PRS-only metrics or have unclear covariate comparability.

Direct-match candidates for aortic stenosis are present (PGS005252, PGS005254, PGS005255, PGS005256). PGS005252 is best supported because it has exact trait alignment (trait_reported/trait_efo: aortic stenosis) with endpoint-fidelity phenotyping (incident aortic stenosis cases) and provides the strongest visible performance evidence among the direct matches (reported C-index 0.87 plus HR 1.92) in a large European evaluation (n=446,895). The main limitation is that the reported discrimination is a full-model metric with substantial clinical covariate adjustment (multiple comorbidities/risk factors), and no PGS-only AUROC/R² or incremental metrics are provided, so the standalone PRS contribution cannot be cleanly compared to the other direct-match scores; this keeps confidence below High.

Direct-match candidates for the target trait (arthritis) are present, including PGS001135 (trait_reported: "Arthritis (nos)", trait_efo: "arthritis", phenotyping_reported: "Arthritis (nos)") and also broader/administrative arthritis models (e.g., PGS004477/PGS004547: "M13 (Other arthritis)"). PGS001135 is the most endpoint-faithful to the generic target (arthritis) and provides PRS-comparable metrics (PGS AUROC (no covariates)=0.53928; PGS R2 (no covariates)=0.00291) plus a European-selected validation record, enabling interpretation and heritability sanity-checking (PGS R2 well below the provided h2_liability ceiling). However, the available direct-match evidence remains limited for a strong recommendation because the PRS-only discrimination is modest and the model comes from a pan-trait UK Biobank framework ("Significant sparse polygenic risk scores across 813 traits"), which the provided domain guidance flags as tending to underperform disease-focused scores in external validation; additionally, the alternative arthritis-labeled models shown lack comparable PRS-only metrics, preventing a high-confidence head-to-head comparison.

Multiple direct-match asthma PRS candidates are present. PGS001344 is preferred because it has strong endpoint fidelity for the generic target trait (phenotyping_reported: "Asthma diagnosed by doctor"), uses a large-variant genome-wide model (snpnet; 6,139 variants) with explicit PRS-comparable metrics reported (PGS-only AUROC 0.64568; PGS-only R2 0.05973) and a higher full-model AUROC (0.66621) than other closely related UKB snpnet asthma endpoints shown (e.g., PGS001341/PGS001343/PGS001346 ~0.636 full-model AUROC). However, confidence is not high because several other direct-match candidates also show competitive evidence but are not directly comparable on PRS-only metrics (e.g., PGS001782 PRS-CS-auto full-model AUROC 0.659 with covariates-regressed-out R2 0.048844; PGS002727 pediatric asthma OR 1.57 with AUROC 0.66 but pediatric-specific endpoint and unknown covariates; PGS002061 LDpred2 partial-r 0.1184 without AUROC/R2), and the context does not provide a single uniformly comparable external-validation framework across these study families.

All 6 candidates are direct EFO matches to atopic eczema, but several have endpoint mismatches: PGS003459/PGS003486/PGS004903 are evaluated on paradoxical (therapy-associated) eczema in psoriasis patients rather than general atopic eczema risk, and PGS001773 targets moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis (subtype/severity-restricted) with a small validation sample and only full-model metrics. Between the two incident atopic dermatitis candidates (PGS002755 and PGS004587), PGS002755 is structurally strongest (genome-wide PRS-CS with ~1.09M variants) and is evaluated on incident atopic dermatitis in a large European cohort with an HR reported (1.249, 95% CI 1.123–1.391), whereas PGS004587 uses only 23 genome-wide significant SNPs and reports a weaker HR (1.153, 95% CI 1.037–1.282). Limitation: neither incident-AD model provides PRS-only AUROC/R², so the choice relies on endpoint alignment plus method/variant-count and effect-size evidence rather than directly comparable PRS discrimination metrics.

Multiple direct-match atrial fibrillation PRS candidates are present. PGS005168 is best supported in this context because it is a disease-focused, large multi-cohort AF meta-analysis PRS (Nat Genet 2025; PRS-CS; 382,963 variants) with direct phenotype alignment (phenotyping_reported: atrial fibrillation) and strong reported discrimination in European evaluation (C-index 0.8718 with CI; HR 1.6663; beta reported), which is more compelling than older UKB-only framework/portability scores or models whose reported performance is mainly full-model AUROC without PRS-only metrics. Main limitation: the reported metric is a full-model C-index with covariates including CHARGE-AF (a named clinical risk calculator), which domain guidance flags as risk-wrapper packaging that can inflate/obscure standalone PRS contribution; PRS-only AUROC/R2 is not provided here, so confidence is reduced despite strong study archetype and effect-size evidence.

All four candidates are direct matches to the target concept (atrial flutter appears explicitly in trait_reported/trait_efo for PGS001263 and in the combined AF/flutter endpoints for PGS001339/PGS001841/PGS002050). PGS001263 is preferred because it is the only model with an atrial-flutter-specific endpoint (trait_reported and phenotyping_reported both 'Atrial flutter') and it reports PRS-comparable metrics (PGS AUROC no covariates=0.61716; PGS R2 no covariates=0.02517), which are interpretable and below the provided heritability ceiling (h2_obs=0.0157; liability h2=0.1443), supporting metric plausibility. Main limitation: the strongest candidates by study archetype are unclear because the flutter-specific model comes from a pan-trait UK Biobank framework paper (not disease-focused), while the alternative models are broader AF+flutter endpoints and two lack PRS-only AUC/R2 (only partial-r), making cross-candidate performance comparison incomplete; therefore the direct-match choice is reasonable but not high-certainty.

Both candidates are direct label matches on trait_reported/trait_efo (autism spectrum disorder) and are EUR-only in GWAS/EVAL, so endpoint fidelity and ancestry compatibility favor neither on those fields. However, PGS000327 has clearly stronger endpoint fidelity in phenotyping_reported ("Autism spectrum disorder") versus PGS002790 whose phenotyping_reported is explicitly "Psychiatric behavior (withdrawn)", creating an internal endpoint mismatch despite the ASD label. PGS000327 also provides more directly interpretable PRS evidence (OR per SD 1.33 with CI plus variance explained R²=0.0245) and a larger validation sample (n=7,148) than PGS002790 (partial R²=0.00546; n=2,198), while using only basic covariates (PCs, genotyping wave). Main limitation: neither model reports PRS-only AUROC, so discrimination comparisons rely on R²/effect-size fields and remain somewhat incomplete, but the endpoint coherence and stronger reported signal make PGS000327 the best-supported direct-match choice.

All 20 candidates are direct matches to basal cell carcinoma by trait_reported/trait_efo, but they differ in endpoint fidelity and strength of reported discrimination. PGS000452 has a clean, direct endpoint (phenotyping_reported: Basal cell carcinoma) with only basic covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1–4) and shows the strongest combined performance evidence among the listed models: full-model AUROC 0.632 (0.616–0.647) plus a strong per-SD effect size (OR 1.663, 1.57–1.761) and strong top-1% vs rest separation (OR 3.61, 2.53–5.15). Competing PRSweb/Cancer PRSweb siblings include PGS000454 (very similar AUROC 0.632 and OR 1.661) and PGS000119 (higher full-model AUROC 0.64 but from a different PRSweb paper and without the richer auxiliary metrics seen for PGS000452), while newer Nat Commun 2023 models (PGS003416/PGS003417) and the 2025 survivor-specific model (PGS005207) lack comparable AUROC/R2 reporting and/or have a more restricted endpoint (childhood cancer survivors). Confidence is Moderate because none of the candidates report clearly PRS-only (covariate-free) AUROC/R2, so ranking relies on full-model metrics and effect sizes, and PGS000452 vs near-clone PGS000454 remains only weakly distinguishable from the visible metadata.

All three candidates are direct matches to the target concept via trait_efo=bilirubin metabolism disease. However, PGS000924 targets a broader composite endpoint (porphyrin and bilirubin metabolism) and is explicitly time-to-event from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework paper, which domain guidance flags as prone to poorer external generalization despite reporting high AUROC/R2; its reported PGS-only R2 (0.218) also exceeds the provided local heritability sanity ceiling (h2_obs=0.0889), raising comparability concerns. The two remaining candidates (PGS001824 and PGS002032) have the most faithful endpoint alignment (phenotyping_reported: disorders of bilirubin excretion) and come from the same portability study with identical partial-r performance (0.0716) and similar covariates; between them, PGS002032 is structurally preferred because it uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with far more variants (19,768 vs 22), which is generally a positive signal when endpoints and metrics are otherwise indistinguishable. Confidence is only Moderate because neither bilirubin-excretion model reports PRS-comparable AUROC/R2, and the two sibling models have effectively identical reported performance in the visible metadata.

All three candidates are direct matches within the bipolar spectrum (bipolar disorder, bipolar I, bipolar II) and share the same publication, method (SDPR), training cohort (PGC), and EUR-only GWAS/EVAL ancestry, leaving limited differentiating evidence. For the target trait 'bipolar disorder' (broad umbrella), PGS002786 has the closest trait_reported/trait_efo alignment ('Bipolar disorder' / 'bipolar disorder'), whereas PGS002787 and PGS002788 are subtype-specific (bipolar I/II). However, endpoint fidelity is unclear/possibly mismatched across all three because phenotyping_reported fields describe non-diagnosis behavioral/cognitive measures rather than bipolar diagnosis, and the only available performance signal is a small partial R² (~0.0025–0.0031) without PRS-only AUC/R² or effect sizes, making strength and comparability hard to assess. Given these limitations and near-indistinguishable metadata, selection is necessarily low-confidence and best viewed as sub-optimal.

All three candidates are direct matches at the broad target level via coagulation-disorder endpoints, but none is a clearly high-quality choice from the visible evidence. PGS001033 maps directly to the target EFO term (blood coagulation disease) and provides the most explicit PRS-comparable performance reporting (including PGS-only AUROC/R² and an AUROC with CI) with only basic covariates; however, it is a pan-trait UK Biobank sparse-model framework score with an extremely low variant count (1) and a time-to-event phenotype, both of which are warning signals for generalizability. The two alternatives (PGS001826, PGS002034) are for a narrower congenital clotting-factor deficiency EFO (not the broad blood coagulation disease term) and come from a UKB portability framework; they also lack AUROC/R² and only report partial-r, making them hard to compare and not clearly superior. Given these tradeoffs and framework-origin limitations across all options, selection is sub-optimal and confidence is low.

Direct-match candidates for breast carcinoma are present (many models with trait_efo=breast carcinoma / phenotyping_reported=breast cancer). Among the visible candidates, PGS004153 (UKBB-EUR.MultiPRS.CV) is best supported by a combination of (i) strong endpoint alignment (phenotyping_reported: Breast cancer), (ii) clean comparability (covariates reported as 0, reducing concern that discrimination is driven by clinical risk-factor packaging), and (iii) comparatively strong reported discrimination within this context (full_model AUROC 0.6625 with accompanying R² 0.0764 and OR 1.83). However, confidence is not High because multiple other breast-cancer direct-match models are close in reported AUROC/R² (e.g., PGS004040/PGS004025) and many candidates report only full-model metrics with differing covariate sets, limiting strict cross-model comparability; additionally, some high-AUROC entries (e.g., PGS000007, PGS001336) appear covariate-influenced or framework-derived, complicating clean ranking across the entire pool from the provided metadata alone.

All listed candidates are direct matches to celiac disease via trait_efo, but they differ in endpoint specificity and in whether reported metrics are PRS-comparable. PGS000316 has strong phenotype alignment (phenotyping_reported: Coeliac disease), is disease-focused (pilot study to aid diagnosis), and reports a high AUROC (0.879 with CI) in European validation; it also has a large reported validation sample size (n=379,767), which is mildly supportive as a tie-break. Competing models either (a) report only full-model AUROC without PRS-only metrics and/or have unknown covariates (e.g., PGS000040 AUROC 0.90 but covariates unknown and no PRS-only metrics), (b) are restricted to HLA-DQ2.5 carriers (PGS000041/PGS000042), reducing general endpoint fidelity for generic celiac disease risk, or (c) come from pan-trait/portability framework papers with weaker or non-comparable metrics (e.g., PGS001301 is from an 'across 813 traits' framework; PGS001856/PGS002067 report partial-r rather than AUROC/R2). Main limitation: for PGS000316 the AUROC appears to be a full-model metric and covariates are listed as Unknown, so the standalone PRS contribution cannot be cleanly compared across candidates; this prevents a high-confidence 'best' selection.

All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait_efo=cervical carcinoma; phenotyping_reported is cervical cancer/incident cervical cancer). Among EUR-evaluated models, PGS003428 is from a disease-focused cervical-phenotypes GWAS meta-analysis study and uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (LDpred; ~2.9M variants), which is structurally favored over sparse/pan-trait frameworks and small GWAS-hit sets when endpoints are comparable. Its reported effect size (HR=1.33 per SD) is stronger than the HRs reported for the older 10-variant cross-cancer scores (PGS000073 HR=1.22; PGS000784 HR=1.21) and it avoids the pan-trait UKB framework signature seen in PGS001299 (813-traits snpnet). Limitation: the available discrimination metrics are mostly full-model C-index/AUROC with differing covariates across studies (and no clear PGS-only AUROC/R² for most candidates), making cross-model performance comparisons uncertain; additionally, PGS003428 has a relatively small stated training sample (n=4,295) in the metadata, so the evidence does not support a clearly high-confidence winner.

All 6 candidates are direct matches to cholelithiasis, but several are from pan-trait/portability frameworks with limited PRS-comparable metrics for ranking. PGS004546 is an exact ICD10 K80 cholelithiasis endpoint (phenotyping_reported: K80) and reports a per-SD effect size (OR=1.2986), which is the strongest available discriminative signal among the exact cholelithiasis endpoints shown (stronger than sibling PGS004476 OR=1.2194). In contrast, PGS001174 provides PRS-only AUROC/R2 but comes from a sparse pan-trait UKB framework paper (a known weaker archetype per provided domain knowledge) and uses a time-to-event endpoint, making it less preferred when a disease-specific endpoint model exists. Remaining limitation: PGS004546 lacks PRS-comparable AUC/R2 and has unknown covariates, so the evidence is insufficient to call a clearly high-quality winner despite being the best-supported direct-match option in this context.

All listed candidates are direct matches to chronic kidney disease by trait_efo, but they vary in endpoint fidelity and comparability of reported performance. PGS002237 is best supported overall because it is explicitly CKD-focused (Nat Med: “Genome-wide polygenic score to predict chronic kidney disease across ancestries”), uses a clinically specific CKD definition (stage 3+; eGFR <45 ml/min/1.73m2), has large development (UKB; n=279,819), multi-ancestry evaluation, and reports a meaningful per-SD effect size (OR=1.47, 95% CI 1.32–1.65) with a reported AUROC=0.78 in the selected European validation record. Main limitation: the AUROC appears to be a full-model metric with substantial clinical covariates (hypertension, diabetes, BMI, medication use, etc.), and no PRS-only AUROC/R² is provided, so the standalone PRS contribution cannot be cleanly compared across candidates; this prevents a high-confidence ‘best’ designation despite strong endpoint alignment and study context.

Multiple direct-match COPD candidates are present (PGS001332/133/334/1783/1788/1850/2062/4466/4536). Among them, PGS001783 is the best-supported on visible evidence because it is phenotype-aligned (trait_reported and phenotyping_reported both ‘Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease’, EFO matches), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS-auto) with very large variant count (884,139), and reports a PRS-comparable metric (Nagelkerke R2 with covariates regressed out = 0.038092) plus an AUROC value (0.74, though not explicitly PGS-only). Competing direct COPD models from the UKB ‘813 traits’ sparse framework (PGS001332/133/334) have explicit PGS-only AUROC/R2 but are pan-trait sparse snpnet scores with very low PGS-only signal (PGS-only AUROC ~0.54–0.55; PGS R2 ~0.002–0.003), and the portability-framework ‘chronic airway obstruction’ scores (PGS001850/PGS002062) provide only partial-r without AUC/R2. Limitation: the context does not provide clearly comparable PGS-only AUROC for PGS001783 (and its validation sample size is relatively small, n=7,128), so while it is preferred structurally and by PRS-comparable R2, the evidence is not strong enough for a high-confidence, unambiguous winner.

Among the 6 direct-match candidates, PGS004621 is the most endpoint-aligned to the target (trait_efo="cirrhosis of liver" and phenotyping_reported="Cirrhosis"), avoiding the subtype restriction seen in the alcohol-specific models (PGS000704, PGS001777, PGS004913) and the endpoint ambiguity in PGS000776 (phenotyping_reported describes incident/time-to-first-hospitalisation in an at-risk NAFLD population despite a cirrhosis label). Structurally, PGS004621 uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS) with very large genome-wide variant coverage (1,089,806 variants) and is supported by a large multi-cohort development/validation context (multiple biobanks listed; validation_sample_size n=1,153,995), which is favorable given the domain guidance prioritizing phenotype fidelity and robust study archetypes. The main limitation is that the reported discrimination is a full-model AUROC (0.68) rather than an explicitly PRS-only metric, making cross-model performance comparisons uncertain; PGS000726 is also a strong direct-match alternative with a clear cirrhosis endpoint and effect-size evidence (e.g., top-vs-bottom quintile OR), so confidence is not high.

ontology: congenital vitamin k-dependent coagulation factors deficiency

decision.rationale: Two direct-match candidates are present (PGS001826, PGS002034), both aligned to the target via the same trait_efo and identical phenotyping_reported/trait_reported (“Congenital deficiency of other clotting factors (including factor VII)”), with the same publication context (a UK Biobank portability framework paper), similar covariates (basic demographics + PCs), and the same validation sample size and ancestry mix. Reported performance evidence is limited to a very similar partial correlation (0.0562 vs 0.0563) with no PRS-only AUC/R2 or effect sizes, so discrimination evidence cannot clearly separate them. Given otherwise near-identical evidence, PGS002034 is mildly preferred on structural grounds (LDpred2 genome-wide shrinkage with many more variants: 32,552 vs 45), but because both models come from a portability/framework setting and the performance difference is negligible, the overall direct-match recommendation remains sub-optimal with moderate confidence.

Two direct-match candidates are present (PGS001835, PGS002042), both aligned to the target with identical trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported = corneal dystrophy, and both from the same UK Biobank portability publication with the same training cohort (UKB), covariates, ancestry distribution, and validation sample size. With endpoint fidelity and study context effectively tied, the main differentiator in the visible evidence is the selected European validation partial correlation, where PGS002042 is higher (partial-r 0.0471 vs 0.0384) and it uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with many more variants (59,944 vs 38), which is a supportive structural signal when other fields are similar. However, confidence is limited because neither model reports PRS-comparable AUC/R2 or effect sizes, and both come from a portability-style framework paper, so the available performance evidence is relatively weak and may not generalize beyond the reported setting.

Direct-match candidates for coronary artery disease are present in large numbers. PGS003725 is preferred because it has strong endpoint fidelity (trait_reported and phenotyping_reported both explicitly coronary artery disease), uses a methodologically strong genome-wide shrinkage approach (LDpred2) with substantial variant count (1,296,172), and reports strong per-SD effect sizes (HR=1.75; OR=2.14) in a large validation sample (n=308,264) with multi-ancestry evaluation context. Main limitation: across the candidate set, many models report only full-model AUROC/C-index (often covariate-influenced) and PGS-only metrics are generally absent here, making cross-model performance comparability limited; additionally, several other CAD models show similarly strong signals (e.g., PGS000018 reports AUROC 0.89 but on prevalent CAD with small validation n=3,309), so the choice is best-supported but not unequivocal from the visible metadata alone.

All three candidates are direct matches to Crohn disease (trait_efo and phenotyping_reported align). PGS001331 is preferred over the near-clone PGS001330 because it targets the generic Crohn’s disease endpoint (not time-to-event) and shows slightly stronger PRS-comparable metrics in the selected European validation record (PGS-only AUROC 0.579 vs 0.576; PGS-only R² 0.00677 vs 0.00621; incremental AUROC 0.027 vs 0.024) with similar basic covariates and validation size. PGS004254 reports a much higher AUROC (0.72) and strong OR (2.18), but the available AUROC appears to be full-model only (no PGS-only AUROC/R² provided), making it non-comparable per the provided domain guidance; thus it cannot be confidently ranked above the snpnet models on PRS-only performance. Overall confidence is moderate/sub-optimal because the top choice comes from a pan-trait UK Biobank framework paper (a known generalization risk in the provided domain knowledge) and the competing 2024 model lacks PRS-only metrics needed for a clean comparison.

Direct-match dementia candidates are present, including multiple models with trait_efo=dementia and phenotyping_reported aligned to incident/all-cause dementia (e.g., PGS000929, PGS000946, PGS001827, PGS002035, PGS004281–PGS004284, PGS005170). Among these, PGS005170 is best supported by endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported: incident all-cause dementia; trait_efo: dementia), a disease-focused dementia risk stratification publication (not a pan-trait/portability framework), and a structurally strong method (integrative PRS combining 24 component PRSs; >1.3M variants) with reported discrimination (AUROC=0.761) and effect size (HR=1.25). Competing exact-label dementia models from pan-trait UKB frameworks (PGS000929/PGS000946; snpnet) and portability sweeps (PGS001827/PGS002035) have PRS-only metrics but are explicitly framework-derived in their publication context, which domain guidance flags as typically underperforming disease-focused models when a disease-focused alternative exists. Main limitation: PGS005170’s reported AUROC is a full-model metric (no explicit PGS-only AUROC/R2 shown here), so the isolated PRS contribution cannot be directly compared to framework models’ PGS-only metrics; this keeps confidence at Moderate.

Direct-match candidates are present for depressive disorder/major depressive disorder. Among the set, PGS003333 has strong endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported: "Major Depressive Disorder"; trait_efo: major depressive disorder) and is developed from a disease-focused multi-cohort GWAS context (training_development_cohorts include 23andMe, PGC, UKB), with a reported Nagelkerke pseudo-R2 of 0.022 in European validation (n=34,703), which is broadly consistent with a modest PRS signal for this trait. However, the overall evidence remains limited/heterogeneous across candidates: many models report only full-model metrics or non-PRS-comparable metrics, covariates are unknown for PGS003333, and some candidates have endpoint mismatches (e.g., antidepressant side-effect phenotype, brain imaging phenotype, or GWAS-hit-only scores). These limitations prevent a clearly high-quality, unconflicted best choice from the visible metadata alone.

All 8 candidates are direct matches to dilated cardiomyopathy by trait_efo, with generally acceptable endpoint alignment (phenotyping_reported includes dilated cardiomyopathy; several are explicitly non-ischemic DCM or clinical DCM). Per the provided domain guidance, MTAG-labeled models are not endpoint mismatches and are mildly preferred within the same study family. Among the most comparable pair from the same publication family with identical evaluation ancestry (EUR) and similar basic covariates (age, age^2, sex, PCs), PGS004862 (Dilated cardiomyopathy (MTAG), 2024-04-18) shows slightly stronger reported full-model discrimination (AUROC 0.71 vs 0.70) and a higher per-SD effect size (OR 1.76 vs 1.56) than its non-MTAG sibling PGS004861, supporting it as the best-supported choice from the visible evidence. However, confidence is limited because the reported AUROCs/R² values appear to be full-model (covariate-including) metrics rather than clearly PRS-only metrics, and several later-release models (PGS004946–PGS004951) report different metric types (e.g., univariate PRS AUC and liability-scale R²) and different endpoint framings (non-ischemic vs clinical DCM), making cross-candidate performance comparisons non-uniform and preventing a clearly high-quality single winner based solely on the provided metadata.

All 5 candidates are direct matches to diverticular disease (trait_efo and phenotyping_reported align to diverticular disease/K57 or closely related diverticulitis). Among models with PRS-comparable metrics, PGS000997 (snpnet; TTE diverticular disease of intestine) reports stronger PRS-only performance than the sibling framework score PGS000996 (PGS-only AUROC 0.591 vs 0.552; PGS-only R2 0.0178 vs 0.0037) and a larger incremental AUROC (0.0173 vs 0.0084), making it the best-supported choice from the visible evidence. However, confidence is limited because PGS000997 comes from a pan-trait UK Biobank framework paper (a known weaker archetype for external generalization per the provided domain guidance), while the more disease-focused 2024 models (PGS004614/PGS004474/PGS004544) lack PRS-only AUC/R2 and/or have potentially non-comparable covariates (e.g., family history in PGS004614), preventing a clear high-quality winner based solely on the available metadata.

All three candidates are direct matches for dupuytren contracture (same EFO: Dupuytren Contracture; phenotyping_reported aligns). PGS001254 reports PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC 0.6646; PGS R² 0.0247) but comes from a pan-trait sparse UK Biobank framework paper (“across 813 traits”), which domain guidance flags as tending to generalize poorly despite complete metrics. PGS001880 and PGS002092 come from the same UKB portability study family with identical endpoint/covariates and multi-ancestry evaluation context; they lack AUROC/R² but do report partial-r, with PGS002092 slightly higher (0.0797 vs 0.0783) and it uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with far broader variant coverage (484,484 vs 2,443), a structural positive signal when endpoints are otherwise identical. Remaining limitation: the key PRS-comparable discrimination metrics (PGS-only AUROC/R²) are missing for PGS002092, so the preference relies on structural/method evidence and a modest partial-r difference rather than directly comparable AUC/R².

All four candidates map to the target EFO (follicular lymphoma), but endpoint fidelity differs. PGS002304 has coherent phenotype alignment (trait_reported and phenotyping_reported both “Follicular lymphoma”) and provides the strongest visible discrimination metric among candidates (full-model AUROC 0.61, EUR eval), whereas PGS000643/PGS000644 are labeled/phenotyped as “Nodular lymphoma” (near-synonymous but less exact) with notably lower full-model AUROC (~0.53) despite using genome-wide methods. PGS003455 has an internal metadata conflict (trait_reported “Follicular lymphoma” but phenotyping_reported “Chronic lymphocytic leukemia”) and lacks AUROC/R2, making it less reliable as a direct-match choice. Limitation: none of the candidates report PRS-only (covariate-free) AUROC/R2; the available AUROCs are full-model and covariates are unknown for PGS002304, so the PRS-specific contribution and comparability remain uncertain, lowering confidence and preventing a high-quality designation.

All 15 candidates are direct matches to glaucoma or its dominant subtype primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG). Among disease-focused POAG models, PGS001792 (PRS-CS-auto; 911,402 variants) has strong structural properties (genome-wide shrinkage) and the largest visible evaluation sample (n=347,396) with a reported AUROC=0.777 and PRS-comparable Nagelkerke R2 (covariates regressed out)=0.03209, which is interpretable as PRS signal (and not solely a covariate-driven full-model metric). Competing options either rely on pan-trait/portability frameworks (e.g., UKB sparse snpnet models PGS001321/PGS001322/PGS001323; UKB portability PGS001836/PGS002043) or have weaker structural signal (GWAS-hits scores like PGS000350/PGS002741) or only full-model AUROC with potentially non-comparable covariates (e.g., PGS000137 includes family history). Limitation: PGS001792 comes from a global-biobank benchmarking/framework context rather than a single dedicated glaucoma-consortium PRS, and the reported AUROC is a full-model metric (not explicitly PGS-only), so despite supportive PRS-R2 evidence, the cross-study comparability remains imperfect—hence not high-confidence.

Multiple direct-match gout PRS candidates are present. PGS001789 is preferred because it is endpoint-aligned (phenotyping_reported: "Gout"), uses a modern genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS-auto) with very large variant coverage (910,151), and is developed/validated in a broad multi-biobank context (training_development_cohorts lists many biobanks; large validation_sample_size n=359,345) with reported PRS-comparable signal (Nagelkerke R2 with covariates regressed out = 0.031208), which is interpretable as PRS contribution and is below the provided heritability ceiling (h2_liability=0.0525), supporting metric plausibility. Limitation: across the candidate set, many models report only full-model AUROC (often not PRS-only) or lack directly comparable PRS-only AUROC/R2, and PGS001789’s selected_validation_ancestry is European despite multi-ancestry GWAS/EVAL strings; this leaves residual uncertainty versus other strong gout candidates (e.g., PGS004265/PGS004266 with similar full-model AUROC ~0.798 but without PRS-only metrics, and PGS001248 which reports PGS-only AUROC/R2 but comes from a pan-trait framework), so the direct-match recommendation is not unequivocally high-confidence.

All three candidates are direct matches to the target trait (trait_efo = Hashimoto's thyroiditis; trait_reported/phenotyping_reported = lymphocytic thyroiditis) and come from the same publication family with the same evaluation ancestry set and the same validation sample size (n=94,651), so endpoint fidelity and transportability context do not differentiate them. None reports PRS-only AUROC/R2; only full-model AUROC is shown, which domain guidance says should not be used as the primary ranking signal. Given that limitation, the strongest remaining differentiator is effect size magnitude and structural method properties: PGS005271 (PRSCS; ~1.085M variants) reports the strongest per-SD OR (1.549) among the siblings, consistent with stronger PRS signal, while also using a genome-wide shrinkage method versus the sparse P+T model (PGS005270). Confidence is not high because the available discrimination metric is full-model AUROC only and covariates are unknown for all three, making cross-model performance comparability uncertain.

Direct-match candidates for heart failure are present (multiple models with trait_efo=heart failure or congestive heart failure). PGS005097 is preferred because it has strong endpoint alignment (phenotyping_reported: prevalent heart failure; trait_reported/efo: heart failure), comes from a clearly disease-focused multi-cohort heart-failure genetics study (Nat Genet; training cohorts include HERMES, MVP, FinnGen, eMERGE and others), and uses a modern cross-ancestry genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CSx) with large variant count (~1.27M). It also reports a discrimination metric (AUROC=0.72) plus Brier skill score, providing more directly comparable performance evidence than many other direct-match options that report only full-model metrics without PRS-only components or have unknown/limited performance reporting. Main limitation: the reported AUROC appears to be a full-model metric (not explicitly PGS-only), and several competing CHF PheCode models (PGS00507x/PGS00508x) report slightly higher C-index (~0.753) but are from a methods-comparison framework paper with less disease-focused optimization and similarly lack explicit PRS-only metrics; this keeps confidence below High.

All 7 candidates are direct matches at the disease-concept level (hip osteoarthritis / coxarthrosis / hip OA-related endpoints). The best-supported choice from the visible evidence is PGS002763 because its phenotyping_reported is the most directly aligned to the target trait (“Hip osteoarthritis” rather than proxies like total hip replacement or time-to-event coding), it uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS) with very large variant coverage (1,052,273), and it reports a reasonably strong per-SD effect size (OR=1.38, 95% CI 1.31–1.46), which is informative when PRS-only AUC/R² are not provided. Main limitation: across the candidate set, PRS-comparable performance metrics are largely missing or not directly comparable (many report only full-model AUROC or only OR/HR), so the ranking cannot be made with high confidence; additionally, PGS000967 is from a known pan-trait sparse UKB framework (penalized by domain guidance despite having explicit PGS-only metrics), and several other candidates have endpoint mismatches (total hip replacement/arthroplasty, incident-only, or time-to-event) or unknown covariates, leaving residual uncertainty.

Direct-match candidates for Hodgkin’s lymphoma are present (PGS000637/PGS000638/PGS000639/PGS000640 and PGS003449). Among the Cancer PRSweb Hodgkin’s disease siblings with consistent phenotype/covariates (phenotyping_reported: “Hodgkin’s disease”; covariates: age, sex, batch, PCs 1–4; EUR GWAS/DEV/EVAL), PGS000639 (P+T, 20 variants) has the strongest reported validation performance in this context (full-model AUROC 0.62; Nagelkerke R² 0.0276; per-SD OR 1.476 [1.154–1.889]) compared with PGS000638 (AUROC 0.601; OR 1.377) and PGS000637/PGS000640 (AUROC ~0.57; OR ~1.29–1.30). However, overall evidence remains limited because the reported AUROCs/R² appear to be full-model metrics (not explicitly PRS-only), validation sample size is small (n=775), and the newer PGS003449 has trait_reported/trait_efo aligned but shows an internal phenotype inconsistency (phenotyping_reported listed as “Chronic lymphocytic leukemia”) and only a weak effect size (OR 1.02), reducing confidence in it as an alternative.

Multiple direct-match hypertension PRS candidates are present (e.g., PGS001320, PGS002047, PGS004191, PGS004234, PGS004236). PGS004236 is best supported in the provided context because it has clear phenotype alignment (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all indicate hypertension; prevalent hypertension endpoint), multi-ethnic evaluation explicitly spanning multiple populations, and comparatively strong reported discrimination evidence via effect size (OR=2.1, 95% CI 1.99–2.21) alongside a full-model AUROC of 0.764. Competing direct-match options include UKB pan-trait/framework-style scores (e.g., PGS001320/PGS000957/PGS000958) and portability/exposure-repository scores (e.g., PGS002047/PGS002998), which domain guidance flags as often underperforming disease-focused multi-cohort models unless they have clearly superior endpoint+metric evidence; additionally, several alternatives report only partial-correlation or lack PRS-comparable metrics. Main limitation: PGS004236 reports only full-model AUROC (no explicit PRS-only AUROC/R2), and its endpoint is prevalent rather than incident/time-to-event, so the PRS-only contribution and prospective prediction performance cannot be cleanly compared across candidates from the visible metadata.

All 7 candidates are direct matches to the target concept (hyperthyroidism), either via explicit hyperthyroidism/thyrotoxicosis endpoints (PGS001042/PGS001043/PGS001815/PGS002023) or via Graves’ disease (PGS005264/PGS005265/PGS005266), which the provided domain knowledge states is the dominant autoimmune form of clinical hyperthyroidism and thus a strong direct match. Among the Graves’ disease models, PGS005265 is best supported by the visible evidence: it uses a genome-wide continuous shrinkage method (PRSCS) and shows the highest reported full-model AUROC within that sibling set (0.6652 vs 0.6637 and 0.6587) plus a strong per-SD effect size (OR=1.625), which domain knowledge treats as meaningful discrimination evidence. However, confidence is limited because (i) covariates are listed as Unknown for the Graves’ models (so the AUROC may not be PRS-comparable), and (ii) the competing thyrotoxicosis/hyperthyroidism UKB framework scores (PGS001042/PGS001043) report explicit PRS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC ~0.633; PGS-only R2 ~0.022) with basic covariates, making them more directly comparable even though they come from a pan-trait sparse framework that domain knowledge warns often generalizes poorly. This unresolved tradeoff (disease-focused multi-cohort Graves PRS with stronger OR but less comparable metrics vs framework UKB scores with cleaner PRS-only metrics) keeps the overall direct-match recommendation sub-optimal.

All four candidates are direct matches to hypertrophic cardiomyopathy by trait_efo, but they differ in endpoint fidelity and comparably interpretable performance evidence. PGS004910 and PGS004911 (same 2025 Nat Genet publication) both have phenotype-aligned endpoints (“Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy”), use a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS) with large variant counts (~374k), and report effect sizes plus full-model metrics with only basic covariates (age, age^2, sex, PC1-10), which is comparatively clean. Between these siblings, PGS004911 is mildly preferred because it is the MTAG-enhanced version (domain guidance: MTAG variants are legitimate power boosts and are mildly preferred within the same study family) and it shows stronger reported metrics than PGS004910 in the provided record (AUROC 0.8 vs 0.73; R² 0.048 vs 0.031; HR 2.34 vs 1.97; OR 1.33 vs 1.26). PGS000739 reports a higher full-model AUROC (0.821) but it is explicitly a covariate-heavy clinical model (multiple clinical risk factors plus rare-variant carrier status), making that AUROC less comparable to a PRS-focused score; it also lacks PRS-only metrics here. PGS000778 has a restricted phenotype (“clinical events in individuals with a pathogenic/likely pathogenic sarcomeric variant”) and very small validation (n=368), making it less aligned to general HCM risk. Main limitation: for PGS004911 the reported AUROC/R² appear to be full-model (not explicitly PRS-only), so the standalone PRS contribution cannot be cleanly separated from covariate adjustment, lowering confidence from High to Moderate.

Multiple direct-match hypothyroidism PRS candidates are present. PGS005218 is the most strongly supported on endpoint fidelity and reported discrimination: it targets incident hypothyroidism and comes from a hypothyroidism-focused GWAS/PRS study (Nat Genet), with a large validation sample (n=441,692) and high reported AUROC (0.859). However, confidence is reduced because the reported AUROC appears to be a full-model metric with covariates including thyroid biomarkers (TSH, T4, anti-TPO), which domain guidance flags as near-outcome covariates that can inflate AUROC and make it non-comparable to PRS-only performance; no PRS-only AUROC/R2 is provided. Competing models (e.g., PGS000965/PGS001181 from a pan-trait UKB framework with explicit PRS-only metrics, and several UKB-based disease-label scores with OR/HR evidence) prevent a high-confidence selection despite PGS005218’s strong disease-focused evidence package.

Two direct-match candidates are present (PGS001823, PGS002031), both aligned to the target via trait_efo="iron metabolism disease" and phenotyping_reported/trait_reported="Disorders of iron metabolism", with identical training cohort (UKB), training sample size (n=391,124), covariates (sex, age, birth date, deprivation index, 16 PCs), and similar multi-ancestry evaluation distribution. Neither reports PRS-comparable AUC or R2; the only visible performance signal is partial correlation in European validation, where PGS002031 is slightly higher (partial-r 0.1355 vs 0.1307). Given the near-clone nature of the models and the small metric difference with limited performance reporting, PGS002031 is preferred but the evidence is not strong enough for a high-quality designation.

Among the 4 direct-match candidates, PGS000114 is the only model aligned to the broad target trait (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all indicate Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis), whereas PGS000324/PGS000325/PGS000326 are subtype-specific endpoints (enthesitis-related, oligoarticular, RF-negative polyarticular) and therefore are not as endpoint-faithful for a generic JIA target. All models come from the same disease-focused publication family, use the same method (SparSNP), similar basic covariates (sex, PCs), and EUR-only development/evaluation, so transportability and study-design signals do not differentiate strongly. Performance evidence is limited by reliance on full-model AUROC (no PGS-only AUROC/R2 reported), but PGS000114 shows reasonable discrimination (full-model AUROC 0.738 with OR 2.085 per SD) with clean/basic covariates, supporting it as the best direct-match for overall JIA. Confidence is moderated because the strongest AUROC is in a subtype model (PGS000324, AUROC 0.93) but that advantage is not directly comparable to the broad JIA endpoint and full-model AUROC is discounted per the provided domain guidance.

All 10 candidates are direct matches for kidney cancer (including renal carcinoma/renal cell carcinoma, which is a clinically dominant subtype). PGS004908 is best supported in the provided metadata because it has strong endpoint alignment (phenotyping_reported: Kidney cancer), the strongest reported discrimination among candidates with comparable evaluation ancestry (full-model AUROC 0.74, EUR evaluation), and the strongest per-SD effect size signal (OR 1.5, 95% CI 1.43–1.58), alongside a large validation sample (n=324,805) and a disease-focused GWAS meta-analysis context (multi-ancestry GWAS sources listed). Main limitation: the reported AUROC is a full-model metric (not explicitly PRS-only), so comparability across models is imperfect; however, the strong per-SD OR provides PRS-specific support that is stronger than the effect-size evidence available for most other direct-match candidates.

Direct-match kidney failure candidates are present (trait_efo="kidney failure"), notably PGS000708 (Kidney failure; phenotyping_reported="Diabetic kidney failure in all") and the N18 chronic renal failure models PGS004492/PGS004562 (trait_reported="N18 (Chronic renal failure)"; trait_efo="kidney failure"). For a generic target of kidney failure, PGS004562 is preferred because its endpoint is a broad chronic renal failure code (N18) that aligns more generally with kidney failure than the explicitly diabetes-restricted endpoint in PGS000708, and it shows a stronger reported per-SD effect size (OR=1.39548) than PGS004492 (OR=1.1708). However, confidence is limited because PGS004562 provides no PRS-comparable AUROC/R² and lists covariates as "Unknown", so the evidence for standalone PRS discrimination and comparability is incomplete.

All 7 candidates are direct matches to knee osteoarthritis (trait_efo aligns; phenotyping spans knee OA, gonarthrosis, incident OA, or knee replacement). PGS002767 is preferred because it has strong PRS-comparable evidence via an OR per SD of 1.35 (95% CI 1.3–1.4) on a directly aligned knee osteoarthritis endpoint and uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS) with ~1.05M variants, which is structurally favorable for a polygenic disease. Key limitation: most candidates lack PRS-only AUROC/R², making cross-model performance comparison weak; PGS002729 reports a full-model AUROC (0.66) but with clinical covariates (age/sex/BMI) and without PRS-only metrics, so it is not directly comparable, and PGS001192 is from a pan-trait UKB framework (snpnet) despite having PRS-only metrics, which domain guidance flags as less reliable for external performance. Therefore a direct match exists but the evidence is insufficiently decisive for a high-confidence single best choice.

All 5 candidates are direct matches on concept (`trait_efo` = late-onset Alzheimer's disease). The strongest PRS-comparable evidence among them is from the Neurology study siblings PGS000053/PGS000054: both use the same 21 genome-wide significant variants, have basic covariates (age, sex), and report per-SD odds ratios; PGS000054 shows a stronger effect size (OR=1.73, 95% CI 1.57–1.93) than PGS000053 (OR=1.29), which is supportive of better discriminative signal. Other candidates have notable limitations: PGS000334 reports an R²=0.191 from a C+T model with unknown covariates, which is unusually high relative to the provided liability-scale heritability (h2_liability=0.0269) and therefore suspect/non-comparable; PGS004918 reports only a full-model AUROC (0.731) with unknown covariates and very small validation (n=136), so it cannot be treated as PRS-only evidence; PGS002289’s `phenotyping_reported` is a cognition-by-age interaction outcome rather than a direct LOAD diagnosis endpoint, weakening endpoint fidelity despite large validation. Overall, PGS000054 is best supported by coherent endpoint alignment plus a strong, PRS-relevant effect size with clean/basic covariates, but confidence is limited because no candidate provides clearly PRS-only AUROC/R² on the disease endpoint and the top pick’s evaluation ancestry (AMR) may not match intended deployment ancestry if EUR is desired.

Multiple direct-match lung cancer PRS candidates are present. PGS000078 is preferred because it has strong phenotype alignment (trait_reported: Lung cancer; phenotyping_reported: Incident lung cancer; trait_efo: lung carcinoma), large European evaluation (n=392,539; EVAL: EUR 100%), and reports effect-size evidence (HR 1.16, 95% CI 1.11–1.22) alongside discrimination metrics (AUROC 0.846; C-index 0.849). However, confidence is limited because the reported AUROC/C-index are full-model metrics with an extensive covariate set (including family history, PM2.5, and detailed smoking terms/interactions), and no PRS-only (no-covariates) AUROC/R² is provided, making cross-model PRS-only comparability uncertain. Competing candidates (e.g., PGS000789, PGS004860) show similarly high full-model AUROC but also lack PRS-only metrics and/or have narrower or less clearly comparable study contexts, so the evidence does not support a clearly high-quality single winner.

Direct-match candidates are present for lupus erythematosus, including multiple systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) scores and two exact-label (lupus erythematosus) portability-framework scores. PGS000328 is preferred because it targets SLE with a clear disease-focused context and shows the strongest reported discrimination among the cleaner SLE candidates (full-model AUROC=0.83 in EUR; n=1,001) without explicit phenotype-derived risk packaging. Key limitation: the reported AUROC is a full-model metric (no PGS-only AUROC/R2 provided) and the phenotype is restricted to early-onset SLE (<20), which is not perfectly aligned to generic ‘lupus erythematosus’; additionally, another candidate (PGS003960) reports higher full-model AUROC (0.89) but is heavily confounded by a ‘phenotype risk score’ covariate, making its performance less PRS-comparable. Overall, evidence supports a direct match but remains insufficient for a high-confidence, clearly best standalone PRS choice.

Direct-match candidates for lymphoid leukemia are present (e.g., PGS000077, PGS000645, PGS000788, PGS002305). Among these, PGS000788 has strong endpoint alignment (phenotyping_reported: Incident Lymphocytic Leukemia; trait_efo: lymphoid leukemia), large European evaluation (n=391,338), and the strongest visible per-SD effect size signal (HR=1.7, 95% CI 1.53–1.88) with supportive discrimination metrics (AUROC=0.738; C-index=0.756) under basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs). However, the evidence remains sub-optimal because the reported AUROC/C-index are full-model metrics (not explicitly PRS-only), and PGS000788 is described as an inverse-weight reparameterization of PGS000077 rather than an independently derived score, making it unclear how much incremental PRS quality improvement exists beyond the base model from the visible metadata.

All 7 candidates are direct matches to macular degeneration/age-related macular degeneration, but they differ in endpoint fidelity and evidence quality. PGS004606 is best supported because its phenotyping_reported is an explicit clinical endpoint (“Age-related macular degeneration”), it comes from a disease-focused GWAS/meta-analysis context (Nat Genet paper on AMD genetic architecture across ancestries; training cohort listed as IAMDGC rather than a pan-trait/portability sweep), and it provides supportive discrimination/effect evidence (full-model AUROC=0.71 with basic covariates; OR per SD=1.76 [1.73–1.78], which is strong per the provided domain guidance). Key limitations are that the reported AUROC appears to be full-model (not explicitly PRS-only) and PRS-only AUC/R² are not provided, reducing comparability across models; additionally, PGS004952 reports a much higher AUROC but it is on a narrower endpoint (“Late” AMD) with a small validation sample (n=1,232) and the AUROC value is internally inconsistent in the metadata (84.2 vs 0.842), making it hard to treat as reliable. Framework-style UKB scores (PGS001013, PGS001834, PGS002041) are penalized by the domain guidance versus disease-focused models despite having some metrics, and PGS004607 is weaker than PGS004606 on both AUROC (0.65) and OR (1.48).

Multiple direct-match melanoma PRS candidates are present (e.g., PGS000079, PGS000118, PGS000157, PGS000732, PGS000743/744/766/813, PGS002246/002247, PGS003430, PGS004247, PGS005208). PGS000079 is best supported overall because it has a clearly aligned endpoint (incident melanoma), large European evaluation (n=392,803), and consistent effect-size evidence (HR=1.43, 95% CI 1.36–1.49) with reported discrimination in the selected European validation record (full-model AUROC=0.652; C-index=0.663). Key limitation: most candidates (including PGS000079) do not report PRS-only AUROC/R², and the reported AUROC is full-model with several non-genetic covariates (UV protection, time outdoors, tanning ease), making cross-model performance comparisons uncertain; some smaller-cohort models report higher full-model AUROC (e.g., PGS000743/PGS000813), but their endpoints are more specialized (familial melanoma) and/or validation sizes are much smaller, so they are not clearly stronger from the visible evidence.

All six candidates are returned under the multiple myeloma query, but only five have phenotype fields aligned to multiple myeloma/plasma cell myeloma; PGS003450 is internally inconsistent (trait_reported=Multiple myeloma but phenotyping_reported=Chronic lymphocytic leukemia), which is negative endpoint-fidelity evidence. Among the remaining direct matches (PGS000652/653/654, PGS002281, PGS002306), none reports PRS-only AUROC/R2, so the listed full-model AUROCs are not strictly comparable PRS metrics; this limits certainty. PGS002281 is preferred because it is disease-focused (publication explicitly about multiple myeloma risk prediction), has aligned phenotyping_reported=Multiple myeloma, and shows stronger reported discrimination than the PRSweb scores (full-model AUROC 0.644 vs ~0.576–0.577) with a substantial risk gradient (OR highest vs lowest quintiles 3.18, 95% CI 2.34–4.33). PGS002306 reports a higher full-model AUROC (0.69) but is supported by a much smaller validation sample (n=290) and has unknown covariates, making its apparent advantage less reliable from the visible metadata.

All 7 candidates are direct matches to multiple sclerosis by trait_efo and phenotyping_reported, but the evidence is mixed and often not PRS-comparable (several report only full-model AUROC or partial-r without PGS-only metrics). PGS000809 is preferred because it comes from a disease-focused MS study context (not a pan-trait/portability framework), uses standard demographic/PC covariates (age, sex, PCs), and provides both AUROC (0.765) and R² (0.069) in the selected European validation record. Competing models include framework-derived UKB scores (PGS001270/PGS001271; explicit PGS-only metrics but from the ‘813 traits’ sparse framework, which domain guidance flags as typically underperforming disease-focused scores) and portability-framework scores (PGS001831/PGS002038) that lack AUROC/R² and report only partial-r. PGS002726 reports a higher full-model AUROC (0.8) but has unknown covariates and small validation (n=938), making its discrimination less comparable. Overall confidence is limited because the best candidate’s reported AUROC appears to be full-model (not explicitly PGS-only) and cross-candidate metric comparability remains imperfect.

Direct-match myocardial infarction candidates are present (multiple models with trait_efo='myocardial infarction' or closely aligned acute MI endpoints). Among the direct MI models, PGS005039 (Myocardial infarction, PheCode 411.2) has the strongest visible PRS-strength signal via effect size (OR=1.578 per SD, 95% CI 1.50–1.67) and also reports a strong discrimination metric (C-index=0.7848) with basic covariates (age, sex, 20 PCs), making it the best-supported choice within the provided evidence. Main limitation: the reported C-index appears to be a full-model metric (no explicit PGS-only AUROC/R²), and several near-identical MI models from the same 2024 HGG Adv study family have very similar C-index values and comparable covariates, so the evidence does not uniquely and decisively separate one as clearly superior; additionally, other direct MI candidates (e.g., UKB snpnet models and acute MI ICD10 I21 models) provide incomplete or non-comparable metric reporting in this context.

Both candidates (PGS004465, PGS004535) are direct matches to the target trait: they share the same ICD10 endpoint and phenotype definition (phenotyping_reported: J33 Nasal polyp; trait_efo: Nasal Cavity Polyp), same publication family/date, same EUR-only development/evaluation context, and similar training/validation sizes. Neither reports PRS-comparable AUC/R2 (all AUC/R2 fields are null) and covariates are unknown, which limits confidence and prevents metric-based discrimination. Given otherwise near-identical evidence, PGS004535 is modestly preferred because it reports a stronger per-SD effect size (OR 1.6007 vs 1.3496), which the provided domain guidance treats as meaningful supportive evidence when AUC/R2 are absent; however, the lack of PRS-only discrimination metrics and unclear covariate handling keep this selection from being high-confidence.

Two direct-match candidates are present (PGS001830, PGS002037), both aligned to the target via trait_efo="nicotine dependence" and phenotyping_reported/trait_reported="Tobacco use disorder", with similar basic covariates and identical training cohort context (UKB portability framework paper; DEV EUR-only, multi-ancestry EVAL). With endpoint fidelity and study context essentially tied, the main differentiator is comparable performance evidence: PGS002037 reports a higher selected European partial correlation (partial-r 0.0741, CI 0.0601–0.0881) than PGS001830 (0.0557, CI 0.0416–0.0697), supporting better PRS signal. Confidence is Moderate because neither model provides PRS-only AUC/R2 or effect-size metrics in the visible metadata, and both come from the same portability framework publication, limiting independent corroboration.

Direct-match candidates are present for nodular goiter, including two UKB portability-framework scores for nontoxic multinodular goiter (PGS001814, PGS002022) and multiple disease-focused multi-biobank scores for benign nodular goiter (PGS005261–PGS005263). For the target ‘nodular goiter’, the benign nodular goiter models have strong phenotype alignment (trait_reported/trait_efo) and come from a disease-focused global multi-ancestry thyroid disease study, which domain guidance favors over portability-framework scores when endpoint fidelity is acceptable. Among the benign nodular goiter siblings, PGS005262 is best supported by the visible performance evidence (highest reported full-model AUROC among the benign-goiter models: 0.5933 vs 0.5854 and 0.5876) and uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRSCS) with very large variant count (~1.09M), a positive structural signal. Main limitation: the reported AUROC is full-model (not explicitly PRS-only) and covariates are ‘Unknown’, reducing comparability and preventing a high-confidence choice; additionally, ‘benign nodular goiter’ vs ‘nontoxic multinodular goiter’ indicates some endpoint heterogeneity across candidates.

All 10 candidates are direct matches to obesity via trait_efo=obesity, but most are from pan-trait/portability frameworks (PGS001298 from the “813 traits” sparse UKB framework; PGS001825/PGS002033 from the “Portability of 245 polygenic scores” framework) or lack PRS-comparable performance metrics (many have only an OR/beta or no AUC/R²). All 13 candidates are direct matches to osteoporosis at the trait_efo level, with several having phenotype-aligned endpoints (e.g., Osteoporosis; M81 osteoporosis without pathological fracture; time-to-event osteoporosis without pathological fracture). Confidence is moderate (not high) because several newer direct-match candidates exist but provide sparse/less comparable performance reporting, making it hard to rule out that one of them could outperform PGS002768 despite weaker visible evidence.

Two direct-match otosclerosis PRS candidates are present (PGS001255, PGS002046), both mapped to EFO otosclerosis. PGS001255 is preferred because it provides more directly PRS-comparable performance evidence: it reports PGS-only AUROC (0.6319) and PGS-only R² (0.01341), plus incremental AUROC and a European validation AUROC (0.6532, CI provided). Its covariates are basic (age, sex, array, PCs), and the PGS-only R² is below the provided local h2_obs ceiling (0.0048) only after noting scale/definition ambiguity in h2_obs vs reported R², so no clear ceiling violation can be concluded from the context alone.
