Main limitation: both models come from UK Biobank framework-style publications (pan-trait sparse SNPnet; UKB portability), and neither is a clearly disease-focused multi-cohort otosclerosis PRS; this lowers confidence and keeps the outcome sub-optimal.

Direct-match candidates are present for the target trait ovarian neoplasm, including multiple models explicitly labeled and EFO-mapped as “Malignant neoplasm of ovary” (ovarian neoplasm) from the Cancer PRSweb study family (PGS000544–PGS000564), plus several closely aligned ovarian carcinoma/cancer models. Among the exact EFO-matched ovarian neoplasm models, PGS000549 has the strongest reported discrimination in its selected European validation record (full-model AUROC 0.567 with the highest Nagelkerke pseudo-R² 0.00996 among the ovarian-neoplasm-labeled set shown, and OR per SD 1.263 [1.15–1.387]), making it the best-supported choice within the exact-label cluster based on the visible metrics. However, confidence is limited because the available AUROC/R² appear to be full-model metrics (not explicitly PRS-only), the PRS effect sizes are only moderate, and there is meaningful competition from ovarian carcinoma/cancer models with higher reported full-model AUROC (e.g., PGS000082/PGS000793) but with a slightly different trait label/EFO mapping than the target ovarian neoplasm.

All 11 candidates are direct matches to pancreatic cancer/pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (target: pancreatic carcinoma), with most mapping to exocrine pancreatic carcinoma and incident pancreatic cancer endpoints. Among them, PGS000083 is best supported by a coherent evidence package: clear endpoint fidelity (incident pancreatic cancer), large European evaluation sample (n=391,491), and moderate per-SD effect size evidence (HR=1.49, 95% CI 1.36–1.62) with reported discrimination metrics (AUROC=0.745; C-index=0.742). Competing models either have weaker reported discrimination (e.g., PGS000385/PGS000386 AUROC ~0.58; PGS004693 AUROC ~0.54), much smaller validation (e.g., PGS000663 n=956), restricted/packaged endpoints (PGS002740 age>70; PGS002264 includes diabetes/clinical risk packaging and has unreported validation ancestry), or lack comparable performance metrics (e.g., PGS000159, PGS004250). However, confidence is not high because the reported AUROC for PGS000083 is a full-model metric with multiple covariates (including family history and smoking/BMI), and no PRS-only AUROC/R² is provided, limiting comparability across candidates and making it unclear how much of the discrimination is attributable to the PRS itself.

All 11 candidates are direct matches at the trait level (Parkinson’s disease), but several are progression-focused endpoints (e.g., cognitive decline, motor decline, Parkinson’s disease dementia) rather than generic PD risk/status, which lowers their endpoint fidelity for the target trait. Among the models with phenotyping_reported explicitly as Parkinson’s disease, PGS000903 (Lancet Neurol 2021 meta-analysis) has strong disease-focused multi-cohort development, a more polygenic construction (C+T; 1,805 variants) than GWAS-hit-only scores, and the richest comparable performance evidence in the provided metadata (reports R²=0.054 and OR=6.25 for top vs bottom quartile, alongside AUROC=0.692). However, the available AUROC appears to be a full-model metric (not explicitly PGS-only), and covariates include age/sex/PCs, so cross-model comparability remains imperfect; additionally, other direct-match alternatives (e.g., PGS000902 from the same publication family) are plausible but have weaker PRS-comparable metrics in the visible fields. These limitations prevent a high-confidence, high-quality designation despite PGS000903 being the best-supported direct-match choice from the context.

All four candidates are direct/near-direct matches to the target concept (peripheral vascular disease), with two labeled as peripheral vascular disease (PGS001843, PGS002055) and two as peripheral artery disease (PGS005158, PGS005217), which is a closely aligned endpoint within the same clinical spectrum. The strongest visible evidence package favors PGS005217: it is disease-focused (JAMA Cardiol: “Polygenic Prediction of Peripheral Artery Disease and Major Adverse Limb Events”), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with a large variant set (1,296,292), has very large multi-ancestry evaluation (n=304,294 across AFR/AMR/EAS/EUR/GME/SAS), and reports a strong PRS effect size (HR per SD 1.66, 95% CI 1.61–1.71). In contrast, the two exact-label ‘peripheral vascular disease, unspecified’ models come from a UKB portability framework paper and only report small partial correlations (0.0151 and 0.0175), which is weak performance evidence despite label match; and PGS005158 is restricted to PAD in type 2 diabetes with a small SNP set (19) and only modest HR (1.13). The overall outcome is sub-optimal rather than high-quality because the selected model’s endpoint is PAD (not explicitly the broader PVD umbrella) and key PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUC/R2) are not provided, limiting cross-model comparability.

All three candidates are direct matches at the EFO level (preeclampsia). Endpoint fidelity favors the Nat Med disease-focused study family (PGS003586/PGS003587) because their phenotyping_reported is explicitly pre-eclampsia/eclampsia, whereas PGS004593 has an internal inconsistency (trait_reported = Preeclampsia but phenotyping_reported = Gestational hypertension), which weakens endpoint coherence despite its large validation sample. Between the two Nat Med siblings, PGS003586 is the cleaner direct match on trait_reported (Pre-eclampsia) and shows a stronger per-SD effect size (OR 1.31 vs 1.20), with otherwise similar method (PRS-CS), covariates (maternal age, age^2, PCs), and evaluation ancestry (EUR). Confidence is not high because none of the candidates report PRS-comparable AUC/R2, so ranking relies mainly on endpoint alignment and effect-size magnitude.

Direct-match candidates are abundant and many have strong phenotype alignment to generic prostate cancer (e.g., incident prostate cancer / cancer of prostate). Among the visible set, PGS004155 (UKBB-EUR.MultiPRS.CV) is a direct prostate cancer model with an explicitly PRS-focused evaluation setup (covariates reported as 0) and strong reported discrimination in its selected European validation (AUROC 0.7049; R² 0.1280) on a large validation sample (n=171,474). It also fits the domain guidance favoring multi-score aggregation/ensemble approaches when available. Main limitation: several closely related models from the same 2023 Am J Hum Genet benchmarking family have very similar endpoints and metrics (e.g., PGS004139 AUROC 0.7003; PGS004042 AUROC 0.6994; PGS004027 AUROC 0.6962), so the advantage is incremental and confidence is moderated by the near-tie cluster rather than a single clearly dominant winner.

Direct-match psoriasis candidates are present (multiple models with trait_efo=psoriasis). Among those, PGS001312 has the cleanest PRS-comparable performance evidence in the provided context: it reports both PGS-only metrics (PGS AUROC (no covariates)=0.69158; PGS R2 (no covariates)=0.05226) and a full-model AUROC with basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs), with a large validation sample (n=67,425) and clear endpoint alignment (phenotyping_reported: Psoriasis). Competing direct-match models either (a) are time-to-event variants with slightly weaker reported discrimination (PGS001313), (b) come from portability/framework studies with only partial-correlation and no AUROC/R2 (PGS001871, PGS002083), or (c) lack PRS-comparable discrimination metrics and/or target severity/sub-phenotypes rather than generic psoriasis status (e.g., PGS004315/PGS004316/PGS00530x). Limitation: the strongest-metric candidate is from a pan-trait UK Biobank framework paper ("across 813 traits"), which domain guidance flags as often less reliable for external generalization than disease-focused models; additionally, several other psoriasis scores lack comparable PRS-only metrics, preventing a high-confidence, evidence-complete head-to-head selection.

Both candidates are direct matches to psoriatic arthritis at the EFO level, with acceptable endpoint alignment (PGS000342: phenotyping_reported=Psoriatic arthritis; PGS001287: phenotyping_reported=Psoriatic arthropathy). PGS001287 has substantially stronger PRS-comparable performance evidence (PGS-only AUROC=0.67648; PGS-only R2=0.0335) and reports incremental/full-model metrics with only basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs), whereas PGS000342 reports only a full-model AUROC (0.562) with unknown covariates and no PGS-only metrics, making its PRS contribution hard to interpret. Main limitation: PGS001287 comes from a pan-trait UK Biobank sparse sNPnet framework paper (a known weaker archetype for external generalization per the provided domain knowledge), so despite better reported PRS-only metrics, the overall direct-match recommendation remains sub-optimal rather than high-confidence.

All 7 candidates are direct matches to pulmonary embolism at the EFO/phenotype level, but evidence quality is mixed. PGS001280 is preferred because it has the cleanest phenotype alignment to the target (trait_efo and phenotyping_reported are PE-specific: "pulmonary embolism" / "TTE PE"), comes with explicit PRS-comparable metrics (PGS AUROC no-covariates=0.60765; PGS R2 no-covariates=0.01403) and basic covariates only (age, sex, array, PCs), and its PRS-only R2 is below the provided EUR heritability ceiling (h2_obs=0.0052; h2_liability=0.1090), supporting metric plausibility. However, confidence is limited because the strongest-endpoint-aligned options are largely from a known pan-trait UKB framework paper ("across 813 traits"), which domain guidance flags as often less externally robust; meanwhile the more disease-focused 2023 Han Chinese model (PGS003861) reports only a full-model AUROC (0.765) with unknown covariates (not PRS-only comparable) and is EAS-only, and the 2024 I26 ICD10 models (PGS004460/PGS004530) lack PRS-comparable performance metrics (only modest ORs shown), preventing a clearly high-quality winner.

Direct-match candidates are present (pulmonary fibrosis / idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis). PGS001791 is preferred because its endpoint is tightly aligned to the target disease spectrum (idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis as a specific pulmonary fibrosis diagnosis), it uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS-auto) with very large variant coverage (910,439), and it is developed across many biobanks with European evaluation reported—an evidence package that is generally more externally robust than a sparse pan-trait UKB framework score. Key limitation: the available PRS-comparable performance evidence is limited (no PGS-only AUROC; only a covariates-regressed-out Nagelkerke R2=0.005929 and a full-model AUROC=0.758), making it hard to confidently separate it from alternatives. PGS001030 has an exact pulmonary fibrosis label and reports PGS-only AUROC/R2, but it is from a known pan-trait sparse UKB framework (snpnet, 51 variants) and its high full-model AUROC appears largely covariate-driven (incremental AUROC 0.01818), reducing confidence. PGS004695 is endpoint-aligned (incident IPF) and reports a strong HR (3.78 high vs low quintile), but lacks standard PRS-comparable AUC/R2 and uses a GWAS-hits-only 23-variant score, leaving uncertainty versus the genome-wide PGS001791.

All four candidates are direct matches to the target trait (retinal detachment) by trait_efo/phenotyping_reported, but they come from two framework-style UK Biobank papers rather than a clearly disease-focused multi-cohort retinal detachment study, which limits confidence in external robustness. Among the two models from the same '813 traits' sparse snpnet framework (PGS000990 vs PGS001137), PGS001137 has the cleanest endpoint alignment ('Retinal detachment' in trait_reported and phenotyping_reported) and stronger PRS-comparable metrics (higher PGS-only AUROC 0.573 vs 0.542; higher PGS-only R2 0.00663 vs 0.00213; higher incremental AUROC 0.0185 vs 0.0061) with similar basic covariates, making it the best-supported choice within the available evidence. The two 'Portability of 245 polygenic scores' candidates (PGS001833, PGS002040) lack PRS-only AUROC/R2 and report only partial correlation, making them harder to compare directly despite slightly higher partial-r for PGS002040; this missing comparability evidence is the main remaining limitation and keeps the overall outcome sub-optimal.

Direct-match rheumatoid arthritis models are present (multiple with trait_efo=rheumatoid arthritis). Among these, PGS004163 is best supported by the visible evidence because it has strong endpoint alignment (phenotyping_reported: Seropositive RA; trait_efo: rheumatoid arthritis) and the strongest reported discrimination within the coherent RA method-comparison cluster from the same publication family (Am J Hum Genet 2023-12-19), with full-model AUROC 0.7469 and R² 0.1376 plus a strong per-SD OR 2.46. Competing direct-match options include UKB pan-trait/framework scores (PGS001309/PGS001310) with notably weaker AUROC (~0.665) and portability/framework scores (PGS001875/PGS002088) that report only partial-r rather than comparable AUROC/R², as well as incident/time-to-event packaging (e.g., PGS004873) that is less directly comparable for generic RA risk. Main limitation: the selected model’s reported metrics are full-model (covariates listed as 0) rather than explicitly PRS-only, and the endpoint is seropositive RA rather than all RA, so while it is a strong direct match, some uncertainty remains about standalone PRS performance for broader RA.

All four candidates are direct matches to sarcoidosis, but two (PGS001872, PGS002084) have a phenotype-mapping inconsistency: trait_efo is listed as "skin sarcoidosis" while the target is sarcoidosis, creating endpoint-fidelity ambiguity despite phenotyping_reported being "Sarcoidosis" and leaving only partial-correlation metrics (no PRS-only AUROC/R²). The remaining two (PGS000922, PGS000923) are clean concept matches (trait_efo="sarcoidosis") and report PRS-comparable metrics including PGS-only AUROC and PGS-only R² with only basic covariates; their PRS-only R² values (~0.017–0.018) are also below the provided heritability ceiling (h2_liability≈0.107), supporting metric plausibility. Between these siblings from the same pan-trait UKB framework paper, PGS000922 is preferred because it targets the generic disease endpoint (phenotyping_reported="Sarcoidosis") rather than a time-to-event formulation (PGS000923), and their performance is very similar (PGS-only AUROC 0.6428 vs 0.6456; full-model AUROC 0.6486 vs 0.6546). Overall confidence is not high because the best-supported options come from a pan-trait sparse-framework study (a known generalizability risk per the provided domain knowledge) and there is no disease-focused multi-cohort alternative in the provided candidate set.

All five candidates are direct matches on trait_reported/trait_efo for schizophrenia, but endpoint fidelity differs: PGS000133/PGS000134/PGS000135/PGS000136 all report phenotyping_reported="Schizophrenia" (direct disease endpoint), whereas PGS002785—despite schizophrenia labeling—has phenotyping_reported="Cognitive function (Cognitive total)", creating an explicit endpoint mismatch for the target trait. Among the four endpoint-faithful siblings from the same publication family with similar basic covariates (age/sex/PCs plus platform/batch), none reports PRS-only metrics; only full-model AUROC and/or per-SD OR are available, which limits comparability and prevents a high-confidence pick. All three candidates are direct matches with identical endpoint fields (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all indicate carcinoma in situ of skin) and similarly basic covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1–4) in EUR-only training/evaluation, so phenotype alignment does not differentiate them. None reports PRS-only AUROC/R2; only full-model AUROC and effect sizes are available, which limits comparability and lowers certainty. Direct-match candidates are present for sleep apnea, including multiple generic “Sleep apnea” models (PGS003204–PGS003218) and several “Obstructive sleep apnea” models (PGS003479, PGS003857, PGS003858, PGS005219, PGS005220). Among OSA candidates, PGS005220 is best supported by the visible evidence: it is a disease-focused OSA PRS with a multi-score aggregation-style method (“weighted PRSsummation PRS-CSs”), large genome-wide variant count (~984k), multi-cohort development (FinnGen, MGBB, MVP), and the strongest available performance signal in this context (full-model AUROC=0.79 plus OR=1.53 per SD), whereas the ExPRSweb “Sleep apnea” framework cluster shows near-null discrimination (full-model AUROC ~0.49–0.53; ORs ~1.0). Main limitation: the reported AUROC is a full-model metric (no PGS-only AUROC/R2 provided) and covariates include BMI (which can affect comparability), so the PRS-only contribution cannot be isolated from the provided metadata; this prevents a high-confidence/high-quality designation despite being the strongest direct-match option shown.

Multiple direct-match candidates are present with consistent phenotype alignment to squamous cell carcinoma (notably PGS000120, PGS000460–PGS000468, PGS000731, PGS005209). Among these, PGS000461 has the strongest visible performance/effect-size evidence within the coherent Cancer PRSweb SCC cluster: full-model AUROC 0.599 (0.579–0.618), the highest Nagelkerke pseudo-R² reported in that cluster (0.0304), and a relatively strong per-SD OR 1.491 (1.395–1.593) with a high top-1% vs rest OR 3.51 (2.29–5.39), while using only basic covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1–4). Direct-match candidates are abundant and many are endpoint-faithful for type 2 diabetes mellitus (trait_efo matches; phenotyping_reported commonly “Type 2 diabetes” or “Incident type 2 diabetes”). However, across the pool, most reported discrimination is full-model AUROC/C-index with heterogeneous and sometimes heavy clinical covariates (e.g., BMI, family history, fasting glucose/lipids), making cross-model performance comparisons non-comparable and often covariate-driven per the provided domain guidance. PGS002308 (PRS-CSx; 1,259,754 variants) is selected as the best-supported direct-match because it is explicitly designed as a trans-ancestry T2D PRS in diverse populations (publication title), reports a PRS-comparable variance metric (R²=0.092) alongside AUROC=0.793, and uses relatively standard adjustment (age, sex, PCs, study site) without obvious near-outcome biomarkers. Limitation: several other direct-match models show higher full-model AUROC/C-index (e.g., PGS001781) or strong effect sizes, but they generally lack PRS-only/comparable metrics and/or use covariate sets that can inflate full-model discrimination; without consistent PRS-only metrics across candidates, the choice remains only moderately certain.

All 5 candidates are direct matches to ulcerative colitis by trait_efo and phenotyping_reported. Outcome is still sub-optimal because the reported AUROC appears to be full-model (no explicit PGS-only AUROC/R2), validation is EUR-only, and cross-study metric comparability remains limited.

Remaining limitation: absence of PRS-only AUROC/R2 for PGS000611 and the presence of several near-tied GWAS-hits/P+T siblings (e.g., PGS000610/PGS000612/PGS000613) means the choice is not definitive.

All 5 candidates are direct matches to urolithiasis or its near-synonyms (urinary calculus; calculus of kidney and ureter; nephrolithiasis/ureterolithiasis). Among the two exact urolithiasis-labeled models (PGS001864, PGS002075) from the same portability framework paper with identical phenotype/covariates and evaluation structure, PGS002075 has the stronger reported PRS-comparable metric (partial correlation 0.0385 vs 0.0323), making it the best-supported choice within the most phenotype-aligned pair. However, confidence is limited because (i) the top candidate’s performance reporting is sparse (no AUROC/R² provided, only partial-r), (ii) the alternative candidates include different endpoint formulations (time-to-event; ICD code N20) with non-comparable or missing PRS-only metrics, and (iii) the leading candidates come from a UK Biobank portability/framework context rather than a clearly disease-focused multi-cohort urolithiasis study, which domain guidance flags as a common source of weaker external generalization.

Direct-match candidates for uterine cancer are present, including exact/umbrella uterine endpoints (PGS000541, PGS000542, PGS001795, PGS003740) and the clinically dominant subtype endometrial carcinoma (multiple models, including PGS003381). Given domain knowledge that endometrial carcinoma is the dominant subtype of uterine carcinoma (~90% of cases), endometrial-cancer PRSs are acceptable direct matches for a uterine-cancer target when better supported. Among the endometrial/uterine-aligned options, PGS003381 (uterine endometrial carcinoma; lassosum; 529,365 variants; EUR GWAS/EVAL; AUROC 0.761 with basic covariates age + top 20 PCs) has strong endpoint fidelity and a genome-wide model with comparatively strong reported discrimination versus other uterine-labeled models that show weaker full-model AUROC (~0.57 for PGS000541/PGS000542) or have very limited validation evidence (e.g., PGS003740 n=372 with only an OR). Limitation: the reported AUROC for PGS003381 appears to be a full-model metric (not explicitly PRS-only), and several other candidates are also plausible direct matches (including exact uterine cancer labels), so the choice is not unequivocally best-supported from PRS-comparable metrics alone.

All three candidates are concept-aligned to vitiligo via trait_reported/trait_efo, but they differ materially in endpoint fidelity. PGS000738 is the most endpoint-faithful option (trait_reported=Vitiligo; phenotyping_reported does not indicate a restricted proxy endpoint), whereas PGS000760 is explicitly tied to a treatment/setting-specific phenotype (anti-PD-L1 induced hypothyroidism in cancer patients) and PGS001536 is a pan-trait UK Biobank framework score with a time-to-event endpoint (TTE vitiligo), both of which are warning signals for generic vitiligo risk deployment. Performance evidence is limited/incomplete across the pool: PGS000738 reports only a pseudo R² (0.0386) and a beta effect size without AUROC/PRS-only metrics; PGS000760 reports an HR=1.41 (moderate) but in a non-vitiligo endpoint context; PGS001536 reports PRS-only AUROC/R² but comes from the ‘813 traits’ sparse framework paper and uses a time-to-event phenotype, which domain guidance flags as less reliable than disease-focused direct endpoints when available. Given these tradeoffs, PGS000738 is best supported on phenotype alignment, but the lack of clear PRS-only discrimination metrics and some metadata ambiguity (phenotyping_reported/covariates not clearly specified) keep the overall direct-match recommendation sub-optimal.
